captions.detailed: A dark gray, grounded upright spine stands on a cross-shaped base. It features three separate branch modules mounted on side saddles at different heights and orientations. The top branch is light gray and ends in a flat pad, the middle branch is olive green and ends in a fork, and the bottom branch is dark blue and ends in a clamp-like tab. Each branch is connected via an independent revolute joint, allowing it to rotate around its respective mounting hub axis.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of a rack-style three-branch rotary tree. It must feature a grounded vertical spine on a cross base, with three independent branches (a light gray pad branch, an olive green fork branch, and a dark blue clamp-tab branch) mounted at different heights. Each branch should be modeled as an independent link with a revolute joint rotating about its side-saddle hub axis.
captions.factory: Construct the main spine using a vertical Box on top of two perpendicular intersecting base plates, topped with a square cap. Create three distinct branch geometries using combinations of Box and Cylinder primitives to form the mounting hubs, extension arms, and their respective end effectors (pad, fork, and clamp tab). Define these as separate parts with distinct colored materials (light gray, olive green, and dark blue), and connect each to the spine using revolute joints with specified rotation axes and limits.
